subject: Immutable audit snapshots — retention and selective erasure window

Subject: Immutable snapshot retention question for SOC 2 review

Hi Soojin,

Quick one as we prep for our SOC 2 assessment next quarter. We need a short, plain-language explanation of how Redwood handles immutable audit snapshots for customer environments: specifically

- How long you retain immutable snapshots that are created for incident forensics or compliance (default retention and any maximum limits).
- Whether customers can request a selective erasure (delete specific snapshot ranges) once a snapshot has been marked immutable.
- If immutable snapshots are replicated across regions and whether deletion requests are region-scoped.

We've prepared an attachment that lists the snapshot IDs we're looking at (audit_snapshot_manifest.csv). Can you confirm what evidence you can provide (hash manifests, chain-of-custody notes, export logs) and an estimated timeline for delivery?

Appreciate a short reply we can attach to our auditor packet.

Thanks,
Samantha Cole
Head of Compliance
Medilab Therapeutics

Attachment: audit_snapshot_manifest.csv (csv)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immutable snapshot retention question for SOC 2 review

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and the manifest. Looping in Kimberly (TAM) and Naomi (Security Evidence Lead) to make sure the reply includes export artifacts. Short answers up front:

- Default immutable snapshot retention: 90 days for forensic snapshots created by customer-initiated retention hold. Standard automated backups/long-term retention are configurable up to 7 years under Private/Dedicated contracts.
- Selective erasure: by design, immutable snapshots cannot be altered. We can initiate a verified deletion workflow for whole-snapshot removal if the customer provides an approved request and the snapshots are not under active legal hold. Partial (range) deletion inside an immutable snapshot is supported only via a compensating workflow that creates a replacement snapshot without the redacted ranges; this is currently a manual operation and requires evidence of authorization.
- Cross-region replication: snapshots may be replicated to a DR region depending on the customer's deployment profile; deletion/removal requests must specify which region(s) to act on. We provide confirmed deletion receipts per-region.

Naomi — can you add the specific evidence artifacts (hash lists, signed deletion receipts, export log paths) and an ETA for delivering those for the IDs in Samantha's manifest?

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immutable snapshot retention question for SOC 2 review

Hi Samantha — following up with the artifacts we can supply and the process notes. For the snapshot IDs you sent we can provide:

- SHA256 manifest for each snapshot (hash_manifest_<id>.txt) showing file-level hashes and a top-level snapshot hash.
- Export log entries (s3://redwood-prod-audit/exports/<id>/export.log) documenting user and service principals that requested the snapshot and the time-of-export.
- Chain-of-custody note: a short PDF describing where the snapshot lived (region, bucket path), retention window, and whether the snapshot was marked immutable.

Process / timeline:
- Standard evidence pull for up to 10 snapshot IDs: 3 business days.
- If a selective-range redact/replace is required, that is a project request: estimate 2–3 weeks calendar to perform a replacement snapshot and provide redaction justification logs.
- Confirmed deletion workflow for whole-snapshot removal (when allowed): we deliver a signed deletion receipt (signed_csr.pdf) within 2 business days after the deletion completes; deletion receipts include per-region confirmation and the deletion job run id.

Notes about SOC 2 / CAIQ implications: CAIQ auditors often ask for retention policy text and a sample deletion receipt; we can supply a short one-page summary that maps these artifacts to the CAIQ/SIG control IDs.

Attachments: requested_evidence_checklist.pdf

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Security Evidence Lead | Redwood Inference

Samantha — quick operational clarifications from TAM perspective:

- Contracted customers on Dedicated or Private can set a max retention outside the 90-day default; the change is applied via config and reflected in the console within 1 hour. We'll need an order change for retention > 1 year (billing/commit).
- For your manifest IDs: I ran a pre-check and two of the snapshot IDs are in a replicated DR region (us-west-2). If you confirm you want deletion across both regions note that we will need a signed deletion authorization from an approved Medilab contact (we accept DocuSign).
- If you want a CAIQ-friendly artifact: I can prepare a one-pager that maps each artifact to CAIQ v3.1 / SIG control names and include a sample deletion receipt.

Suggested next steps:
1) Samantha to confirm which snapshot IDs require deletion or redaction (if any).
2) If deletion: provide DocuSign authorization or identify the signer.
3) Naomi to start evidence pull for the non-deletion artifacts (hash manifests + export logs).

Happy to run a 20min call this week if useful.

—Kimberly
